items.title: 68357_Jimmy Maxwell oral history interview
items.q: We had Charlie Shavers, Teddy Wilson, Al Hall, Specs Powell and Trummy Young.

ctx.x: that. What was that you were telling me about, an opposite story about what had happened to you before and what happened to you when you were with Redd Foxx?

Oh, yeah, going back to that story with the Chesterfield story and, you know, taking that case up to the union. While -- it reminds me of other stuff, too. First, while we were at the union these guys were saying, well, it's not that we're prejudiced against the black guys. But you know how it is, the black guy's a jazz musician, he can't read. And, you know, they're troublemakers. And Feinberg said, "Well, I've got a white, Anglo-Saxon man sitting here, Protestant -- he didn't know I'm not a protestant, who…

So repercussions went on through the years but the nicest one was 20 years later, I was playing at the Apollo Theater with Quincy Jones and Redd Foxx was the star, Billy Eckstine and Redd Foxx. And the last night -- well, Redd Foxx always kidded me, looked back and called me "The Lord," because

items.title: 68357_Jimmy Maxwell oral history interview
items.q: But after Charlie died he used to come around. I'd see him every once in a while because he always kind of liked me.

ctx.x: I'm trying to think what I knew -- you remember Crip used to come around.
Yeah, that's who it was. But after Charlie died he used to come around. I'd see him every once in a while because he always kind of liked me.
